text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Heart surgeries were put on hold in Vilnius and Kaunas for two weeks and in Klaipeda for nearly two months because hosipitals ran out of the necessary materials.
- The constitutional court decided on Thursday that the decision of parliament to form a new council of national television and radio in December was unconstitutional.
- Lithuania's Economy minister Vincas Babilius met the representatives of Russia's Jukos oil company which is mulling buying into the share issue of the Butinges oil terminal.
- Lithuania's parliament decided on Thursday to authorise the government to take control of sea oil transit in emergency situations to satisfy the needs of the economy.

- The statistics department of the Bank of Lithuania said that there were only six private deposits exceeding 500,000 litas, three of them exceeding 2.9 million litas, in the country's banks. The officials said that other rich people either do not keep their savings in the country's banks or invest their money abroad.
- A group of Turkish businessmen arriving together with the country's president on Monday will hold meetings with Lithuanian businesses and companies.
- Lithuania's commercial banks issued 1.777 billion litas worth of loans in litas and 72.8 million litas in foreign currencies in April.
